non_blocking_notes: The defensive 'LOW' risk branch is unreachable given the closed indicator set, but it serves as a safe default if the indicator set is expanded in the future without updating the classification logic.
The audit log payload explicitly includes 'deployment': 'DISABLED' and 'response_executed': False, which strongly reinforces the non-executing nature of the finding.
proposed_rules: Ensure that any new indicators added to _INDICATORS have corresponding protocol/direction consistency checks and risk classifications to maintain the closed-set invariant and fail-closed behavior.
result.reasoning_summary: The implementation correctly adheres to the acceptance criteria for FW-NET-003. It classifies only exact admitted facts deterministically without consulting a model. The risk levels (MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL) and recommendations (WARN/PROPOSE_BLOCK) are fixed and derived from the indicator set. The code fails closed on empty, malformed, contradictory, cross-tenant, authority-shaped, or Evidence-failing inputs. No live network access, mutation, containment, deployment, or response executor is introduced. The tests cover the deterministic behavior, rejection of invalid inputs, and revalidation of tenant/authority/evidence. The precedence of risk classification is correct (CRITICAL > HIGH > MEDIUM). The protocol/direction consistency checks are appropriate for the specific indicators (e.g., UNAUTHORIZED_EGRESS requires OUTBOUND, LATERAL_MOVEMENT requires EAST_WEST, SMB_WRITE requires SMB protocol, DNS_ANOMALY requires DNS protocol). The frozen dataclass ensures immutability of the finding. The audit call is wrapped in a try/except to deny on failure, ensuring evidence integrity.
tests_missing: Test for NETWORK_PROBE with direction constraints (if any exist, though currently no direction constraint is applied to it in the code)
